name: Daily new job postings from target companies to Google Sheets

parameters.content:
## Daily new job postings from target companies to Google Sheets

### How it works
Every morning this workflow reads the career sites of the companies you list (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workable, SmartRecruiters, Recruitee and Personio boards) and appends only the jobs that appeared since the previous run to a Google Sheet. Useful for recruiters tracking hiring at client companies, sales teams watching for expansion signals, and job seekers.

It uses the [Career Site Jobs Scraper](https://apify.com/ninoventures/career-site-jobs) actor on Apify. You give company domains; the actor finds the job board itself. With "only new jobs" on, it remembers what it returned before, so rows aren't duplicated. The first run fills the sheet with all current openings that match your filters.

### Setup
1. Create an Apify account and copy your API token.
2. In **Fetch new jobs**, create a Header Auth credential: name `Authorization`, value `Bearer YOUR_TOKEN`.
3. Create a Google Sheet with a tab named `Jobs` and this header row: Found on, Company, Title, Department, Location, Remote, Salary, Posted, Link, Board.
4. Connect Google Sheets in **Append jobs to sheet** and paste the sheet URL into **Settings**.
5. Set the companies and optional title and location keywords in **Settings**.

### Cost
$1.50 per 1,000 jobs. Filters run before charging, so excluded jobs are free.

### Customization
Add a Slack step after the sheet, or set `remoteOnly` to true.

## Configure
Companies, keyword filters and the sheet URL.

## Get new jobs
The actor finds each company's job board and returns only postings it hasn't returned before.

## Write to the sheet
One row per new job. Salary is filled only when the company publishes it.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ companies: $json.companies.split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean), titleKeywords: $json.titleKeywords.split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean), locationKeywords: $json.locationKeywords.split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean), remoteOnly: $json.remoteOnly, onlyNewJobs: true, monitorName: $json.monitorName }) }}
